column2: W4 GEMV kernels (src/gemv.cu): gate|up, qkv|z, q|k|v, o_proj, down run at 740-825 GB/s against ~880 GB/s for a pure streaming read and are ~79% of a step; at T=5..8 the mma tile count grows (more B columns per weight pass), at T=1..4 it does not. GEMV_LOG.md lists every failed attempt (L2 prefetch of the next layer, evict-first policy, tile layouts alone, config sweeps, w16/KS/U variants, scale-layout alone): do not repeat them. The only measured lever left there is the full repack (#10: -0.2 ms T=1, -0.45 ms T=4; touches pack.py, pack_mtp.py, prefill.py dequant, tests); also try other levers (split-K for o_proj, scale handling, epilogue fusion, tail-wave / launch overhead, T>4 variants that keep the stream rate).

DeltaNet at verify widths up to 8: the step writes T state snapshots into the 9-slot ring (state traffic (1+T) x 3.15 MB per layer, 0.51 ms at T=1 -> 1.14 ms at T=4 -> 2.00 ms at T=8 for 48 layers, 678 GB/s; the T=8 tail cycle costs +2.5 ms over a T=4 cycle and DeltaNet is 44% of that growth). Look for ways to avoid writing snapshots the accept rule will discard (write only rows that can be accepted, lazy replay / recompute of the accepted rows' state after accept, in-place update with rollback data, bf16 snapshots of rows >= 4), plus the conv ring and the accept kernel's slot bookkeeping. The ring must stay exact (forced acceptance up to 8 rows and ring wrap are checked).

Full-attention decode (src/attn.cu), 16 layers: prep + split-KV + reduce are 3 launches per layer, ~7 us fixed per layer at 2K-8K context (about 0.1 ms/step if fused); at 8K context the KV read is 0.78 ms (bf16). T>4 tiles: T=5 runs 4 n-tiles x KS=2 warps, T=6..8 5..6 n-tiles x KS=1, a 6-warp block per kv head that is latency bound (T=8 at 8K 1.09 ms vs 0.88 at T=4; fp8 T=6 jumps 0.62 -> 0.92 ms); a wider split needs 320-384 threads and a 170-204 register cap against 238 used (spills). Prep / reduce fusion, split counts, better KV streaming, tile shapes for T=5..8.

Small kernels and launch structure inside the CUDA graph: 129 RMSNorm launches (0.37 ms), in_proj_a|b, DeltaNet, conv, attention prep/split/reduce, embed, argmax, the accept kernel, the result-mailbox kernel of the hybrid cycle. BENCH.md records that fusing RMSNorm into the GEMV prologue was slower (+5.3 us per GEMV); fusions into epilogues, kernel-count reduction, graph-level concurrency (forked branches like in_proj_a|b) and removing launch gaps are open; every cycle width T = 4..8 has its own graph, so a launch-structure win must hold at T=4 and T=8.

MTP cycle overhead outside the verify GEMVs (1.55-1.63 ms per cycle): catch-up of the accepted rows (k+1 padded rows through the MTP layer, 0.32-0.36 ms; with the tail the catch-up still covers k+1 rows), the chained drafts (0.43 ms each: MTP layer 0.21 GB + 64k int4 head 0.17 GB), the accept kernel (greedy and sampling), the mailbox report, the host proposer loop (src/pld.cu, 3-5 us per cycle) and sync grouping (spec.py cycles_pld). Ideas: cheaper draft path that keeps the draft distribution, overlapping drafts with the tail of verify, catch-up on fewer rows, a leaner accept kernel.

lm_head path (src/head_q.cu, K9): an int4 head copy (0.78 ms GEMV at T=1) selects the top-R candidates of every verify row and exact BF16 dots rescore them (BENCH.md K9: -2.05 ms/step); the BF16 head stays resident for the rescoring; with verify widths up to 8 the head GEMV and the select kernel run on up to 8 rows. Open: cheaper selection tail (~50 us per call), 4..8-row head GEMV efficiency, int4 rows layout / scale handling, skipping rows that cannot change the accept decision (rows behind a certain rejection), a smaller R when the margin allows, keeping the exactness contract (test_headq.py).

Verify-width policy of the hybrid draft: the proposer (E6's best cell: n=2 longest suffix match of the chain's last two drafts, agreement >= 3, tail <= 4, <= 64 candidates; src/pld.cu, make_pld in spec.py) vs the cost of the extra rows (V(8) - V(4) = 2.0-2.3 ms, a tail cycle is +12%): 5 / 6-row widths are never used with a 4-token tail, the 8K prose prompt loses 2% because 12% of its cycles carry a tail that rarely lands. Open: cost-aware tail length (shorter tails for low agreement), context-dependent gate, match-reliability from the MTP draft confidences, which rows to verify, T=5/6 widths. Constraints: the output must stay exact (greedy and speculative sampling), the adaptive back-off by EMA of the tail's gain was already a dead end (BENCH.md K11); the held workload contains PLD-friendly and PLD-hostile prompts.

Whatever `try --profile` suggests: start from the kernel table (ms per cycle) for the code, long8k and edit prompts, pick the largest item that no other lineage is working on and that BENCH.md / GEMV_LOG.md do not already list as a negative result.
